solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: My clue cooked up for Aristotle's school

indicators.note: food cooked up is prepared from raw ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of having concocted a clue fit for an ancient Greek academy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked up' rearranges the six letters of MY CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lyceum was the Athenian gymnasium where Aristotle taught, giving its name to his Peripatetic school.

clue.text: Peer that goes without golf throughout a number of months

indicators.note: the other pieces go outside, around, the nobleman

parts.note: yon is an old word for that, over there
an earl is a peer of the realm
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A nobleman manages without golf for months on end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes without' looks like doing without; here it means going outside. 'that' as YON is archaic, as in 'yon hill'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearlong means lasting a full year, and a year is twelve months, so it fits loosely.

clue.text: Printing unit, sound and arousing jealousy

parts.note: an en is a unit of measurement in printing, half an em
a sound plan is viable, workable

explanation.surface: A printing machine in good condition makes rivals envious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enviable is so desirable that it makes others covet it.

clue.text: Ordinal produced by philosopher in hot resort

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was an English philosopher

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means sort again, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A philosopher is spotted at a hot holiday destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday spot; read as re-sort it rearranges IN HOT into IONTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Millionth is the ordinal number corresponding to one million, giving position in a sequence.

clue.text: Small cup offered by girl in sanctimonious family

indicators.note: the girl's name is placed in the middle of the word for sanctimonious

parts.note: pi is informal British for piously self-righteous
Ann is a girl's name
kin means one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: A girl from a holier-than-thou household hands someone a little cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannikin is a small metal drinking vessel or pan, a dated term for a little mug.

clue.text: Food for people with shares?

parts.note: people with shares sound like shareholders, but the shares are ploughshares, so these are farmhands and this is their meal

explanation.surface: A question about catering for company shareholders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shares' suggests stock-market investors; it is short for ploughshares, the blades of a plough.
explanation.definitionFit: This British pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle is named after farm labourers who work with a plough.

clue.text: Most elegant farm animal is French

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, an ox or cow
est is French for is

explanation.surface: The smartest beast on the farm turns out to be French.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatest means tidiest and most trim, so it is a synonym of most elegant.

clue.text: Sweetener giving defensive player stimulation at first

indicators.note: at first puts the word for stimulation ahead of the player

parts.note: a kick is a thrill or stimulation
a back is a defender in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A defender gets a buzz early on from something sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A kickback is an illicit payment to secure a deal, a bribe known informally as a sweetener.

clue.text: Old Scandinavian identifies chap from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue read from the south means read from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: to name someone is to identify them
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A Viking picks out a man who came up from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'from the south' means reading upwards, so the pieces are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norseman was a native of ancient Scandinavia, especially a Viking.

clue.text: Book written in African state, primarily on Shakespearean steward

indicators.note: the book's abbreviation is written inside the name of the African country

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
vol. is the abbreviation for volume, a book

indicators.note: primarily picks out only the opening letter of the word on

explanation.surface: A book set in an African country leads with a study of a Shakespeare character.
explanation.definitionFit: Malvolio is Olivia's pompous steward in Twelfth Night, gulled by the forged letter.

clue.text: Reindeer in peril, about to be substituted for good

indicators.note: the letter for about takes the place of the letter for good in the word for peril

parts.note: danger is a synonym of peril
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A reindeer in danger is about to be swapped out for a better one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to be substituted' reads as one phrase on the surface; cryptically 'about' is C and 'to be substituted for good' swaps it in for the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancer is one of Santa Claus's reindeer named in the poem A Visit from St Nicholas.

clue.text: Attractive grassy areas used in first half of game

indicators.note: the grassy areas are put to use inside the shortened game name
only the opening half of the game's name is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: ping-pong is table tennis
leas are meadows or grassland

explanation.surface: Pleasant meadows are pressed into service for the opening half of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pleasing is agreeable or appealing, which is a synonym of attractive.

clue.text: Exercise gets first of bulky blokes losing eight stone

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: A gym programme helps big men shed eight stone of weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eight stone' reads as a weight lost; cryptically 'eight' supplies just its first letter and 'stone' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pebble is a small rounded stone, typically worn smooth by water.

clue.text: At home this person's invested in fast pain relief

indicators.note: the pieces are placed within the word for the fast, as money is put into something

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
in means at home
this person is the speaker, I, and this person's is I'm, I am

explanation.surface: Someone at home puts their faith in a quick remedy for an ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speedy relief, but it is the noun, a period without food.
explanation.definitionFit: A liniment is a medicated lotion rubbed on the skin to ease aches and stiffness.

clue.text: Greet journalist protecting usual extremists? That's knotty

indicators.note: the greeting surrounds and shields the letters from usual

parts.note: to nod at someone is to greet them

indicators.note: the extremists of a word are its two end letters

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Someone acknowledges a reporter who shields the usual radicals, a thorny problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' looks like militants; it takes the ends of 'usual'. 'knotty' means having knots, not tricky.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodulated means covered in nodules, small knobbly lumps, which is a literal sense of knotty.

clue.text: Monster involved in rather gory comeback

indicators.note: a comeback returns, so the letters found are read in the opposite direction
the letters are wrapped up inside the words rather gory

explanation.surface: A monster stars in a fairly gruesome return to the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' picks ERGO from 'rathER GOry'; 'comeback' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, the archetypal fairy-tale monster.

clue.text: Unacceptable mendacity? Not near the centre

parts.note: out can mean not acceptable, as in that's out
mendacity is untruthfulness, lying

explanation.surface: Telling lies is beyond the pale, far from the middle ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlying means situated far from a central point, remote or peripheral.

clue.text: Aussie native taking tea with male fellow lodger

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, native to Australia
maté is a South American herbal tea

explanation.surface: An Australian takes tea with a man who shares his digs.
explanation.definitionFit: A roommate shares a room or lodgings with another, so is a fellow lodger.

clue.text: A type lacking finish is similar

indicators.note: the word for type is missing its last letter, its finish

parts.note: kind means type or sort

explanation.surface: A sort of thing without polish resembles something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking finish' drops the D from KIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means related or of a like nature, so it is a synonym of similar.

clue.text: Scope revealed by Oscar, standing in in goal

parts.note: ambit means scope or extent

indicators.note: Oscar is standing inside the second in

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Oscar winner's range shows as he deputises between the posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing in in' looks like a stutter: 'standing in' is the containment indicator and the second 'in' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambition is something one strives to achieve, an aim or goal.

clue.text: Popular mason disturbed about current sleep disorder

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the current
disturbed means the letters of mason are shaken into a new order

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A well-liked builder, upset about recent events, cannot sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges MASON to SOMNA, which goes 'about' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is habitual inability to sleep, the commonest sleep disorder.

clue.text: Article by Catholic dignitary about an Anglo-Saxon responsibility

indicators.note: the definite article goes about, around, the word an

parts.note: the is the definite article
taken as written
Dom is a title given to some Catholic monks and dignitaries

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece beside a Catholic official discusses a duty from early English history.
explanation.definitionFit: A thanedom was the land and office held by a thane, a nobleman of Anglo-Saxon England.

clue.text: Money divided by male soldiers in that place

indicators.note: the word for money is split apart by the other pieces placed inside

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money
he is the male pronoun
RE is the Royal Engineers, army soldiers

explanation.surface: Cash is shared out between the men of a regiment stationed somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is a formal adverb meaning within that place or thing.

clue.text: Bovine bloke protecting posh legislator

indicators.note: the bloke's name surrounds and shields the other pieces

parts.note: Len is a man's name
U denotes upper-class, posh usage
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A dull-witted man shields an upper-class member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bovine' looks like a cow, but here it means slow and stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Bovine figuratively means sluggish and dim, and lumpen likewise describes the dull, unthinking mass.

clue.text: Old man with money picked up something to suck

indicators.note: with places the father after the money in the answer
picked up means heard, so the sound of the word for money is wanted

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money
pop is an informal word for father, the old man

explanation.surface: An old fellow with some cash buys himself a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: LOLLY (British slang for money) said aloud gives LOLLI, followed by POP.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a boiled sweet on a stick, made to be sucked.

clue.text: Girl presented by one's second son

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I's, I is
Abel was the second son of Adam and Eve

explanation.surface: A girl is introduced by someone's younger boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabel is a girl's name, the Spanish form of Elizabeth.

clue.text: Sustenance teachers finally sought, eating nothing in Paris

indicators.note: the outer pieces swallow the French word, as if eating it

parts.note: NUT is the National Union of Teachers

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of the word sought

parts.note: rien is French for nothing

explanation.surface: Teachers at last look for food while dining on nothing in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrient is a substance providing nourishment, so it serves as a synonym for sustenance.

clue.text: He reigns ineptly, though fairly committed to environment

indicators.note: something done ineptly is botched and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A king rules badly, though he is rather keen on green issues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ineptly' rearranges HE REIGNS; the -ISH ending gives 'fairly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means environmentally conscious, and the suffix -ish softens it to somewhat so.

clue.text: Laid back about English knight's disclaimer

indicators.note: the turned-round letters go about, around, the other pieces
back means the word laid is read from end to start

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A relaxed English knight issues a statement denying responsibility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LAID into DIAL, which goes 'about' E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A denial is a statement refusing to accept or admit something, which is what a disclaimer does.
